resources.string: One thing from Kaaga to pick up or coming up, with Later to bring it back when you can act; or your day.
This link isn\'t a Kaaga connect link. Make a new code in Settings → Phone app.
For an address on the internet, Kaaga needs https. Check the address in Settings → Phone app.
Couldn\'t reach Kaaga at %1$s. Until Kaaga is online, the phone needs your computer on and the same Wi-Fi or hotspot, or the USB cable.
Kaaga didn\'t accept this phone\'s code just now. The app keeps it and tries again; if it keeps happening, make a new one on your computer in Settings → Phone app.
This phone\'s code was ended. Make a new one on your computer in Settings → Phone app.
This code can\'t read the picture. Make a new one in Settings → Phone app.
Kaaga answered with an error (%1$d). The app tries again in 15 minutes.
Kaaga sent something this app can\'t read. Build and install the latest app.
The phone didn\'t accept the wallpaper. Try Refresh now.
The home screen keeps the last picture. Pick another wallpaper in the phone\'s settings.
The lock screen keeps the last picture. Pick another wallpaper in the phone\'s settings.
The home screen shows the phone\'s own wallpaper again.
The lock screen shows your home wallpaper again.
Your reminders from Kaaga, at their time, with sound.
Reminders that ring: a full-screen alarm with sound until you snooze or dismiss it.
Notifications are off for this app. Turn them on in App info.
Kaaga left you a note. Open the app to read it.
When Kaaga leaves you a new note: at most two a day, never in quiet hours.
A question now and then, without a sound: answer with a tap or a few words, or let it go. It leaves by itself at its time and in quiet hours.
Kaaga has a question. Open the app to see it.
Open the app to connect this phone.
Later: bring this back at a time you can act on it
The picture of your day, with small icons for your notifications on the lock screen.
Google sign-in can\'t open inside the app. Sign in with your email and password (on the website, Forgot password sets one).
Kaaga needs the internet. Check your connection, then try again.
